analyst.summary: SRF had a strong FY26 (year to Mar-2026), with profit up nearly 47% on the back of its Chemicals business - particularly firm global prices for refrigerant gases (HFCs). Revenue growth was more modest at about 7%, because the packaging-films and technical-textiles businesses (roughly half the company) are still working through a China-driven global oversupply cycle that has capped their growth and margins. The balance sheet is strong (low debt, top-tier credit rating, no promoter share pledge), and management has laid out a large multi-year capex plan (~Rs 3,900 crore) to expand refrigerant-gas and specialty-chemical capacity. The catch: the stock trades at close to 47 times last year's earnings, which already assumes this pace of improvement continues for several years - a big ask given the very jump in profit last year was flattered by a low prior-year base and a favourable pricing cycle that may not persist. We rate this a Hold: a genuinely improving business, but priced for a best case that leaves little room for the packaging-films drag to persist or the chemicals pricing cycle to cool.
